attributes.provenance: src/game/sfx/sfx.c::ProcessEffects (worktree GDL-Claude-SfxMatch2, work_claim.sfx-processeffects-2.20260831.v1, attempt.processeffects-frame-pad-fix.20260829.v3): two verified instances. (1) enemy grid-collision do-while: `if (e->flags & 0x400) { if (maxtime-remaining>0.0667) hit=-1; } else { <~35-insn vel/hitcount/NormalVector/damage_enemy/PlayerDamagedEnemy body> }` -- target places the ~35-insn body as the unconditional fallthrough and the 6-insn hit=-1 check as a far branch target reached only via a taken `bne`; our then-current source (small body textually first) compiled with the opposite layout (small body inline, big body jump-away). Inverting to `if (!(e->flags & 0x400)) { <big body> } else { <small body> }` (De Morgan, zero semantic change) reproduced target's layout exactly, closing an 8-subcluster/~90-target-insn mismatch region to 2 residual instructions. (2) movement-position chain: `} else if ((e->flags&0x4000) && (e->flags&0x8000)) { pos=oldpos (3 stores, ~9 insns) } else { <vel-based movement + drag, ~25 insns> }` -- same pattern, same fix (`!(A&&B)` inversion), fully aligned a 68-row fnasm --diff window (12 mismatched rows -> 0), net-real-neutral (a cascade elsewhere absorbed the local gain, still not a regression). A third test on a plain ternary (non-block) EXPRESSION, `hit = damage == 0 ? 2 : 3` rewritten to `damage != 0 ? 3 : 2`, produced a byte-IDENTICAL compile (zero effect) -- the lever only fires when the two arms are genuine STATEMENT bodies MWCC must lay out as separate basic blocks, not a scalar ternary expression (which MWCC canonicalizes to one fixed branch polarity regardless of source spelling).
attributes.scope: MWCC GC 1.2.5 family with the per-TU flags in configure.py; applies to an `if (cond) { A } else { B }` (or the final arm of an if/else-if chain) where A and B are genuine statement bodies (not a scalar ternary expression) of visibly different instruction-count size, and target's disassembly shows the LARGER body as the unconditional fallthrough with the SMALLER body relocated to a branch-only-reached target.

subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: For an `if (cond) { A } else { B }` statement (or the final `else`/`else if` arm of a longer chain) where A and B are real statement bodies of visibly different size, MWCC's default basic-block layout places whichever arm is written FIRST (textually, as the `if`-true body) as the fallthrough path reached without a branch, and the other arm as a target reached only via a taken conditional branch -- independent of which arm is objectively larger. When target's disassembly instead shows the LARGER body as the fallthrough and the SMALLER body relocated to a far branch target, the current source has the two arms in the wrong textual order relative to target's chosen layout. Fix: negate `cond` (De Morgan: `!(A&&B)` from `A&&B`, or a plain `!flag` from `flag`) and swap the two arm bodies verbatim, so the arm target places as fallthrough becomes the textual `if`-true body again. This is a zero-semantic-change, purely mechanical transformation, gated with fndiff/probe.py like any other source-shape change. Boundary (verified negative): the lever does NOT apply to a simple ternary EXPRESSION assigned to a scalar (`x = cond ? valA : valB;`) -- MWCC evidently canonicalizes a ternary's branch polarity independent of source spelling (verified: `damage == 0 ? 2 : 3` and the algebraically-inverted `damage != 0 ? 3 : 2` compiled to byte-identical output). It applies specifically when the compiler must emit A and B as separate basic blocks (multi-statement bodies, or any body containing its own control flow/calls), not when it can fold a scalar choice into one merge point. Diagnostic: in an fndiff --ops cluster spanning a whole if/else region, if EVERY instruction in both arms shows up as an insert/delete/replace (not just the branch opcode itself), and one arm is visibly larger than the other, check which arm is fallthrough in target vs which is fallthrough in ours before looking for any other cause -- an arm-swap is the cheapest lever to try first for this shape. Companion to claim.law.independent-statement-reorder-matches-target-schedule (which reorders adjacent independent STATEMENTS for scheduler interleaving) and claim.law.declaration-initializer-split-controls-entry-schedule (which is about a declaration's initializer vs. an earlier store) -- this law is about which BASIC BLOCK an if/else compiles to fallthrough-first, a distinct branch-layout mechanism from either.
